story.title: Tadej Pogacar Claims Fifth Tour de France Title, Matching All-Time Record
story.summary: Tadej Pogacar of Slovenia has won the 2026 Tour de France, marking his fifth victory in the prestigious cycling event. This win ties him with four other cyclists for the most Tour de France titles in history. The final stage saw Mathieu van der Poel take the stage win, while Pogacar's overall performance contributed to the race being the fastest edition ever recorded.

explore_lenses.label: How did Pogačar build such a decisive win?
explore_lenses.title: Stage wins and team depth drove the margin
explore_lenses.summary: Pogačar combined five stage victories with a UAE Team Emirates-XRG support group that controlled key mountain and transition stages. The final 6:26 margin over Remco Evenepoel was also shaped by Jonas Vingegaard's Stage 15 withdrawal.

claims.text: Pogačar won five stages and finished the Tour in 73:56:26, 6:26 ahead of runner-up Remco Evenepoel.
On Stage 19, UAE used Félix Großschartner to set the chase and Adam Yates as a rider ahead of the favorites before Pogačar attacked 12 km from the Alpe d'Huez summit and won solo.
Vingegaard, who had been second overall, withdrew on Stage 15; Pogačar said the race would not be the same without his long-running rival.

explore_lenses.label: What does the fifth title change?
explore_lenses.title: He joins the five-win record holders
explore_lenses.summary: The victory moves Pogačar from four Tour titles into a five-rider tie for the record, while also reinforcing UAE Team Emirates-XRG's depth through Isaac del Toro's podium and youth-classification win.

claims.text: Pogačar now shares the record of five Tour de France victories with Jacques Anquetil, Eddy Merckx, Bernard Hinault and Miguel Indurain.
Isaac del Toro finished third overall, 9:42 behind Pogačar, and won the young-rider classification; the official Tour report says he was the first Mexican to finish on the Tour podium.
Pogačar said he now needs to find a new goal, rather than identifying a specific immediate target.

explore_lenses.label: What is Pogačar's next competitive step?
explore_lenses.title: The Vuelta is possible, not confirmed
explore_lenses.summary: The next Grand Tour, the Vuelta a España, is scheduled to begin on August 22, but Pogačar did not commit to starting it after the Tour. He has won the Giro d'Italia but not the Vuelta, making it a potential—though unconfirmed—next objective.

claims.text: The 2026 Vuelta a España is due to start on August 22, and Pogačar said of taking part: “Let's see.”
Pogačar won the Giro d'Italia in 2024 but has not won the Vuelta, according to AP's post-race report.
Pogačar expressed hope that Vingegaard and other riders who crashed out could recover so they could compete again next year.

related_stories.title: FIFA President Infantino Defends World Cup Amid Criticism
related_stories.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has responded to critics of the World Cup, accusing them of being 'consumed by hate' and spreading false narratives. In a strongly worded statement, he suggested that detractors should 'meditate, pray or watch a football match' instead of perpetuating negativity. Infantino defended the tournament as a celebration of unity, safety, and inclusion, dismissing concerns about corruption and disciplinary rulings.

related_stories.title: Severe Wildfires Force Mass Evacuations in France and Spain
related_stories.summary: Over 300,000 people have been evacuated from their homes in France and Spain due to severe wildfires that have been raging for several days. Fire crews are struggling to contain the unpredictable blazes, which have been exacerbated by an impending heatwave.

related_stories.title: Oil Prices Decline as US and Iran Pause Strikes for Diplomatic Efforts
related_stories.summary: Oil prices fell on Monday following a pause in strikes between the US and Iran, which has raised hopes for renewed diplomatic talks. The US halted its attacks after 13 days, with officials indicating that this pause is intended to create 'space' for negotiations regarding the Strait of Hormuz.

related_stories.title: Elizabeth Smart Expresses Hope for Missing Nancy Guthrie 25 Weeks After Abduction
related_stories.summary: Elizabeth Smart, a kidnapping survivor, has stated that there is still hope for the safe return of Nancy Guthrie, who has been missing for 25 weeks following her suspected abduction from her home in Tucson, Arizona. Investigators are also looking into a possible ransom note related to Guthrie's case.
